profile.name: Okanlawon
profile.headline: Clear design makes products brighter.
profile.intro: I'm a UI designer in Ibadan. Small, careful details in every screen add up to apps and websites that look sharp and feel easy to use.
profile.bio: I design clean, polished interfaces for mobile apps, websites and dashboards. I care about layout, typography, colour and the small details that make a screen feel finished, with a soft spot for products built for African users.

services.title: Mobile app design
services.description: Polished app screens, from the first screen to a clickable prototype.

services.title: Website & landing page
services.description: A marketing site that looks great and shows off your product.

services.title: Dashboard & product UI
services.description: Clear interfaces for data-heavy tools, admin panels and SaaS products.

principles.title: Details make the difference
principles.text: Spacing, alignment and type are checked on every screen, so the whole product feels polished.

principles.title: Clarity over decoration
principles.text: If a detail doesn't help someone understand or act, it goes.

principles.title: Design for real conditions
principles.text: Small screens, slow networks and busy days. Designs should still work there.

principles.title: Systems, not one-offs
principles.text: Reusable components and styles keep products consistent and faster to build.

principles.title: Clean handoff
principles.text: Organised files, named layers and documented states, so developers build what was designed.

works.title: AgrovanT
works.summary: A mobile app that helps Nigerian farmers plan, protect and sell their crops, in English, Yorùbá or Pidgin.
works.description:
THE PROBLEM
Most farming advice in Nigeria is written for researchers, not farmers. It is in English, uses kilograms per hectare, and ignores the local weather. Prices change from market to market, and a sick crop often goes unnoticed until it is too late.

WHO IT'S FOR
Small and medium farmers in South-West Nigeria who grow cassava, maize, yam and vegetables. They use mid-range Android phones, often outdoors in bright sun, and many prefer Yorùbá or Pidgin.

SCREENS I DESIGNED
• Onboarding that asks for a language before anything else.
• A home screen built around today's work: weather advice and tasks from the farmer's planting plan.
• Crop guides that show local names next to English, with planting windows, spacing and growth stages.
• A fertiliser calculator that answers in whole 50 kg bags, not kg per hectare.
• A crop doctor that diagnoses a leaf photo, shows how sure it is, and always offers a call to a human extension officer.
• Market prices that are checked before they show, plus Ask Agro, an assistant for text or voice questions.

KEY DECISIONS
Light, high-contrast screens that stay readable in the sun. Large tap targets of 44 px or more. Every tool is two taps from home, so the camera sits in the centre of the tab bar. Advice is written as an action ("Apply fertiliser after the rain passes"), not as raw data.

DESIGN SYSTEM
Colours taken from the farm: Forest, Leaf, Sun and Soil, with a warm cream background. Bricolage Grotesque for headings and DM Sans for body text, chosen because it supports Yorùbá tone marks.

PROTOTYPE
The clickable Figma prototype covers the main journeys: onboarding to home, crop doctor to diagnosis, market prices, the fertiliser calculator and Ask Agro. The screens are built with reusable components, colour and text styles, and auto layout.

NOTE
Prices, weather and the diagnosis shown in these screens are example data used for the design.
